description: Adopt an off-the-shelf OpenAI-compatible multi-provider gateway (LiteLLM) as the leaf model-backend, replacing the hand-built provider-router where it merely duplicates commodity functionality, while keeping agora's genuine differentiators. The provider-router is a LEAF capability (per ADR-0001): a single model-backend ladder reached over the wire and exposed as a KCB capability, distinct from the inter-participant discovery registry — so swapping its internals does not touch the registry. LiteLLM is that same category (OpenAI-compatible across many providers, fallback chains, per-request/per-key hard budgets, cost tracking). This tasklist is deliberately SPIKE-GATED: nothing migrates until a spike verifies LiteLLM actually covers agora's needs. The differentiators that must survive any swap are (1) the always-completes, zero-spend deterministic PLACEHOLDER bottom rung (a fresh install answers immediately, spends nothing, and can never fail), (2) exposing the gateway as a KCB capability via its AgentCard/manifest, and (3) per-request budget ceilings that skip any tier whose projected cost exceeds the ceiling WITHOUT dialing it. The mlx-serve and local/Ollama tiers must remain reachable. Anti-fabrication rule: a migration story passes only when the area gate is green AND the behavior is actually verified end to end (e.g. a real zero-budget request lands on the placeholder tier); an unverified swap never counts as a pass, and any need the spike finds uncovered is DOCUMENTED as a gap rather than forced.
warmup: ls provider-router-erl/test/apr_conformance_SUITE_data && python3 -c "import litellm" 2>/dev/null || echo 'litellm is not yet a dependency — the spike adds and evaluates it'

userStories.title: Spike: does LiteLLM cover the leaf gateway's needs?
acceptanceCriteria: A written spike report (committed under docs/, e.g. docs/spike-litellm-leaf.md) records, feature by feature, whether LiteLLM covers each agora leaf-gateway need: the always-completes deterministic-placeholder bottom rung (zero-spend default), the mlx-serve tier, the local/Ollama tier, per-request budget ceilings that skip an over-ceiling tier without dialing it, and cost estimation per tier/modality.

For each need the report gives a verdict of COVERED (with the LiteLLM mechanism that provides it), COVERED-WITH-A-THIN-SHIM (naming the shim), or NOT COVERED (describing the gap and what agora must keep hand-built).

The report states an explicit go/no-go per downstream story (US-2, US-3): a migration story proceeds only if its prerequisites are COVERED or shimmable; otherwise that story is redefined to DOCUMENT the gap instead of forcing the swap.

The spike is grounded in runnable evidence, not claims: at minimum a throwaway script demonstrating LiteLLM answering an OpenAI-compatible request and demonstrating a budget ceiling being enforced (or the report records that it could not be demonstrated and why).
No production code is migrated in this story and every existing area gate (make check-provider-router, make check-router-erl) stays green.

userStories.title: Front LiteLLM behind agora's OpenAI surface, preserving the zero-spend placeholder tier and KCB exposure
acceptanceCriteria: GATED ON US-1: proceed only if the spike cleared the placeholder, mlx-serve, local, budget-ceiling, and cost-estimation needs; if any was NOT COVERED, this story instead lands the documented shim/keep-decision for that need and says so in its commit.

The provider-router's OpenAI-compatible surface delegates model-backend dispatch to LiteLLM for the tiers LiteLLM covers, while agora keeps ownership of the always-completes deterministic PLACEHOLDER bottom rung so a keyless install still resolves every request to the free tier and never fails.

A request carrying a zero budget ceiling (X-Agora-Budget-Units: 0) is verified to land on the placeholder tier and cost nothing, and a request whose only affordable option is a cheaper tier falls through without the over-ceiling tier being dialed — demonstrated by a test, not asserted.
The gateway is still exposed as a KCB capability: its AgentCard/manifest is served and validates against the schemas package, so a peer can discover and dial it exactly as before.
make check-provider-router and make check-schemas pass (and make check if more than one area is touched).

userStories.title: Retire or repoint the dual Erlang/Python router and its conformance corpus — only if the spike cleared it
acceptanceCriteria: GATED ON US-1 and US-2: proceed only if the spike confirmed LiteLLM covers the behaviors the byte-identical Erlang/Python dual router encodes; otherwise this story documents precisely which router behaviors must remain hand-built and stops there.

The now-redundant hand-built router internals are retired or repointed to the LiteLLM-backed path, with the conformance corpus (provider-router-erl/test/apr_conformance_SUITE_data + the console fixtures/scenarios that replay it) either frozen as the historical contract record or updated to assert the new implementation's external contract — never left asserting a code path that no longer runs.
The provider-router-roundtrip conformance scenario still passes end to end (discover through the registry, dial the address, zero-budget request served for nothing by the always-completes tier).

The external wire contract is unchanged for callers: the same OpenAI-compatible routes, /doctor, /health, /v1/models, /v1/providers, the AgentCard, and the same AGORA_* configuration behave identically, verified by the retained/updated conformance assertions.
make check passes (this story spans provider-router and console), with zero gate errors.
